newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya to cut spending, raise revenue for IMF loss.
newsitem.headline: Kenya to cut spending, raise revenue for IMF loss.

text.p: Kenya 's finance minister said on Friday the government would cut expenditures and raise revenues to cover a $141 million shortfall caused by the IMF halting a key aid package.

'The government will concurrently cut its expenditure for this year and take revenue measures sufficient to address the shortfall of $141 million in external funding,' minister Musalia Mudavadi said in a statement.

Mudavadi said the government wanted to assure the public it was committed to maintaining economic stability in the face of the IMF decision would open talks on a possible "shadow" programme that would set targets for Kenya to meet for the aid.
He said before the IMF decision to halt the aid package the government had expected a total of $141 million to support the current budget from the IMF and from other multilateral donors.
Another $74 million had been expected from the IMF in this financial year to support the foreign exchange market, he said.
Mudavadi says market forces should prevail on the
shilling but without compromising the aim of stable prices in the face of the IMF halting payment of $74 million to back the balance of payments.

'The impact of the shortfall of $74 million will have to be addressed by market forces in both the foreign exchange and the domestic market money without compromising the objective of maintaining price stability', Mudavadi said.

Mudavadi said on monetary policy the government remained committed to price stability and stability of the financial system despite losing the $74 million from the IMF to support the foreign exchange market.

He said the loss of the $74 million, and another $141 million that Kenya had been expecting from the IMF and other multilateral donors to support the current budget, could destabilise the economy if appropriate fiscal and monetary steps were not taken.
